title: `jnp.std` returns `inf` instead of `nan` for float32 arrays near overflow
author: AjBrown89

comments.author: jakevdp
comments.body:
Thanks for the report – I think this is working as expected. `jnp.std` is computed as the square root of the variance, and the variance here is +inf when working at float32 precision.

NumPy's computational model is different: internally it will generally compute things at float64 precision, and this can lead to different numerics in the extreme. For what it's worth, NumPy returns inf in the similar case when operating at the limits of float64 precision:
```python
>>> x = np.array([-1.79769313e+308, 1., 1., 1.79769313e+308])
>>> np.std(x)
/.../numpy/_core/_methods.py:190: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in square
np.float64(inf)
```
I'm going to close this, because I think it's working as expected.
